summary: All four blocking spec review findings are valid and require small spec repairs before gate.

items.title: runtime-log retrieval can select its own just-opened block
items.rationale: The finding identifies a real self-selection loop for flow get runtime-log because automatic logging opens before command execution.
items.evidence: spec.json R1 covers every flow command and R9 selects the latest active-flow block by default, but no exception or snapshot rule exists for flow get runtime-log.

items.title: no-flow logs have no retrieval contract
items.rationale: The replacement diagnostic workflow must work before an active flow exists because prepare and resume can fail in no-flow state.
items.evidence: spec.json R2 stores no-flow output in .tmp/logs/no-flow.log, while R9 only names active-flow default selection and runId#sequence selection.

items.title: finalize-cleanup metadata timing is unresolved
items.rationale: finalize-cleanup removes active state after committing flow.json, so generic post-dispatch metadata persistence cannot safely update the finalized step.
items.evidence: spec.json clarification includes finalize-* as step-associated commands without a finalize-cleanup-specific exception.

items.title: report show failure bypasses dispatcher finalization
items.rationale: Direct process.exit would prevent the dispatcher from writing endedAt and exitCode to the runtime log block.
items.evidence: source review found src/flow/lib/run-report-show.js catches errors, writes process.stderr, and calls process.exit(1).
